Businesses selling organic produce would need an organic certificate from an issuing body, renewable every 12 months, with an exemption for resellers who do not alter the goods or packaging. A transition period of 3 years from Royal Assent is provided, and an independent review is required after 6 years of operation.. Businesses that sell or import organic goods in Australia, including resellers and importers, as well as consumers.

title: Electoral Legislation Amendment (Fair Territory Representation) Bill 2024
snippet: before parliament. This bill would give the Australian Capital Territory and the Northern Territory fairer representation in the Senate. It would set the number of senators for each territory at half the number for a state, rounded to the nearest whole number. Each territory would elect three senators at every federal election, and those senators would serve six-year terms.. Voters and senators in the Australian Capital Territory and the Northern Territory.

title: Whistleblower Protection Authority Bill 2025
snippet: before parliament. The bill would create a new independent federal agency called the Whistleblower Protection Authority to help whistleblowers. The Authority would provide information, advice, assistance, guidance and support, receive and facilitate investigations of disclosures, investigate mistreatment of whistleblowers, and carry out enforcement and education activities. The Authority would have jurisdiction over all federal whistleblower protection laws and consist of a Commissioner, Deputy Commissioners, a Chief Executive Officer, and staff, along with an Advisory Board and a Parliamentary Joint Committee.. Whistleblowers and potential whistleblowers under federal whistleblower protection laws.

title: Defence Trade Controls Amendment (Genocide, War Crimes and Crimes Against Humanity) Bill 2024
snippet: lapsed. This bill would stop Australian-made defence goods, technologies and services from being exported if they could be used in genocide or similar serious international crimes. It would ban exports to a foreign country when the International Court of Justice has ruled that country poses a real and imminent risk of harming a people's right to be protected from genocide. The bill would also apply when Australia knows or should know of a serious risk of genocide, including after a provisional measures order from the International Court of Justice.. Exporters of Australian-made defence goods, technologies and services.

title: Genocide Risk Reporting Bill 2024
snippet: lapsed. This bill would stop Australian government money from going into businesses linked to genocide or that hide or ignore genocide risks. It sets up yearly public reports from certain companies and groups on how they deal with genocide risks in their supply chains, and creates an Anti-Genocide Commissioner to help businesses and government follow the law. The commissioner would lack the power to investigate or force disclosure, and the bill introduces criminal and civil penalties based on recommendations from a review of the Modern Slavery Act 2018, plus judicial review for some ministerial and commissioner decisions.. Australian businesses and entities with operations or supply chains that might involve genocide risks, especially large companies with complex global supply chains, and also government entities that invest in or procure from such businesses.

title: Tertiary Education Legislation Amendment (There For Education, Not Profit) Bill 2025
snippet: before parliament. The bill would cap the pay of Australian university vice-chancellors at $430,000 a year. It would amend the Australian National University Act 1991 to apply the cap to the Australian National University and the Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency Act 2011 to require other public universities to comply. The Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency (TEQSA) could obtain information from universities about vice-chancellor pay, and the minister could prescribe a different amount by legislative instrument subject to parliamentary disallowance.. Australian public universities and their vice-chancellors, particularly the Australian National University.

title: Remuneration Tribunal Amendment (There For Public Service, Not Profit) Bill 2025
snippet: before parliament. The bill would cap the pay of senior government executives and public office holders at $430,000 per year. It would amend the Remuneration Tribunal Act 1973 to require the Remuneration Tribunal to set remuneration below that limit, unless the responsible minister prescribes a higher amount by legislative instrument subject to parliamentary disallowance. The limit would take effect the day after the bill receives royal assent and would apply to determinations made on or after that date.. Australian Government department secretaries, holders of public office, and holders of principal executive office.

title: Lobbying (Improving Government Honesty and Trust) Bill 2025
snippet: before parliament. This bill would tighten rules on who can lobby the federal government and what they must disclose. It would expand the lobbyist register, ban unregistered lobbying, require quarterly reports of meetings, publish ministers' diaries, and extend the ban on former ministers lobbying to three years. The National Anti-Corruption Commission would be able to investigate breaches, with penalties including fines and suspension or cancellation of registration.. Professional lobbyists, in-house lobbyists, former ministers and senior government officials and advisers, and government representatives.

title: Constitution Alteration (Right to Free Speech) 2025
snippet: before parliament. This bill would add a right to free speech to the Australian Constitution. It would insert a new chapter and section barring the Commonwealth and states from making laws that limit free speech, including press and media freedom. The change would take effect only if approved by a majority of all eligible voters nationally and in a majority of states at a referendum.. The change would affect all Australians, including the press and other media.
